newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom's China future still uncertain.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom's China future still uncertain.

text.p: Months of talk about a Chinese partner for Hongkong Telecom may have ended with China Telecom's purchase of a stake in the company, but analysts say years of uncertainty may follow with benefits to Telecom still unclear.
"The China market is huge but there are a lot of uncertainties," HSBC James Capel analyst David Gibbons told Reuters on Tuesday.
"The structure of the deal has raised the question over the extent that Telecom will benefit from China opportunities."

Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd's parent Cable and Wireless Plc said on Friday it had agreed to sell a 5.5 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom to China Telecom, which is controlled by China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT).

C&W said it may also transfer more Hongkong Telecom shares to China Telecom -- with a view that both China Telecom and C&W become equal shareholders -- but only if this enhanced value for shareholders and if important mainland projects were realised.
With only a small stake in Hongkong Telecom, analysts said MPT was likely initially to favour China Telecom (Hong Kong), a vehicle to develop the market in China and in Hong Kong.

"There will be an incentive for the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications to develop China Telecom (Hong Kong) at the expense of Hongkong Telecom," said Fredson Bowers, director of Asia telecoms research at W.I. Carr.
He said there was little to get excited about in the near term, with the benefits to Hongkong Telecom likely to be seen in the medium to longer term.

"The first step is for China Telecom to increase its stake to equal that of Cable and Wireless before they will use Hongkong Telecom," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities. "It will take some time before that happens."
Analysts said China may also take some time to open up its domestic telecommunications market, where foreign companies are currently restricted from direct participation.
While China may restructure its foreign investment laws to offer China Telecom (Hong Kong) early entry, Hongkong Telecom would need a broader market opening, said Bowers.
The rewards for Hongkong Telecom were also uncertain, with any possible investments in China likely to take years to yield any returns.
"It is likely that the initial impact on earnings will be negative. In terms of earnings contributions, it is several years off," said Gibbons.
But analysts said China would have to offer Cable & Wireless a carrot to continue selling down its stake in Hongkong Telecom.

"As MPT sells assets to China Telecom (Hong Kong) and as that business is built up, you at the same time will see Cable & Wireless further divesting Hongkong Telecom shares," said Bowers. "That would broadly correspond to a reasonable timeframe for the opening of the China telecommunications market."

He said as China Telecom increases its stake in Hongkong Telecom, "the incentive for China Telecom to favour China Telecom (Hong Kong) will ease over time and there will be greater incentive to develop Hongkong Telecom".
Hongkong Telecom shares tumbled HK$1.65, or 8.68 percent, to HK$17.35 on Tuesday as the deal fell short of investors' euphoric expectations. The stock gained 10.8 percent last week.
"The developments are in the price and further upside is contingent on further developments in China," said Gibbons.
Analysts said a future listing in Hong Kong of China Telecom (Hong Kong) was also likely to prompt some switching.
China Telecom said on Tuesday it expected to list the Hong Kong subsidiary in the near future.
"China Telecom (Hong Kong) is quite likely to produce a very big draw for investment. It is likely that investor interest will be attracted away from Hongkong Telecom," said Gibbons.
